provenance: Synthetic evaluation-only passages and queries, authored for this benchmark; labels are provisional and not externally or independently human-reviewed.

passages.text: The Juniper battery stores 20 kWh of electricity and operates in Bristol.
Juniper battery inspections are required every 30 days. The maintenance team records each inspection.
The Cedar wind turbine produces 50 kilowatts at rated wind speed and is installed in York.
The Maple solar array has 40 photovoltaic panels with a total peak capacity of 16 kilowatts.
The Birch water reservoir holds 900 litres and supplies irrigation water to the east garden.
The Willow heat pump has a seasonal coefficient of performance of 3.8 and heats a library in Bath.
The Oak electric shuttle carries 18 passengers and runs between the station and campus every 15 minutes.
The Juniper charging station requires 45 minutes to add 10 kWh under standard conditions.
The Cedar battery safety enclosure is inspected every 30 days; this schedule does not apply to the Juniper battery.
The Maple solar array is located in York. Its panels face south.
The library heated by the Willow system opens at 9:00 and closes at 17:00 on weekdays.
The Oak shuttle route is 6 kilometres long. Its 15-minute service interval is measured between departures.
Copyright law regulates the reproduction and distribution of protected creative works.
Fair use analysis considers purpose, nature, amount used, and effect on the potential market.
Trademark law protects signs that distinguish the goods or services of one business from another.
A laboratory report describes a 22 kWh prototype battery tested in Bristol; it is a prototype, not the Juniper installation.
